items.title: 56799_Red Norvo oral history interview
items.q: Johnny Carlson was the first trumpet player... I was rooming with him... we worked in a place near Detroit... a year's contract at the Mirror Ballroom in Detroit.

ctx.x: Yeah, he's never given up. And he -- my mother, said well Glenn's still after him, so he came up and -- to Chicago again, and talked to me and I said, 'Well if by chance maybe I can do it.' So at the end of that summer, in August, I worked with -- had a band was formed, I think, out of Minneapolis. And, we worked in a place near Detroit. And the band was very good, we had arrangements and everything going for them. So, we got a call-- a year's contract at the Mirror Ballroom in Detroit. I thought this is perfect,…

why don't you register?" I said, all right, maybe I will. He said, I'll drive you out. He had a car. We got up the next morning, I went out to the University of Detroit, I applied, they took me and I went to -- I started school. College. AT the University of Detroit. And I was -- I had three 8:00 o'clock classes. A week and worked in a ballroom till 1:00. Everynight. Besides studying, doing rehearsals, used to do all these things.
